## Load the predictions and means data


```{r}
years <- c("2019", "2024")

# Load the means and distibution data which covers all years
ACS_1year_means <-read.csv(file.path(input_means))
```

## Calculate the number of HH in each category 
```{r}


years <- c("2019", "2024")

# Probabilities just list the probability of an average household belonging to
# each income category.  Here they are multiplied by the number of households
# in San Diego that year to produce counts of the number of predicted HH per bin
# new df are produced for each model which insert "HH" before the year

for (yr in years) {

  assign(
    paste0("predict_logit_HH", yr),
    get(paste0("predict_logit_", yr)) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          -YEAR,
          ~ .x * ACS_1year_means$NHH
        )
      )
  )
  
  assign(
    paste0("predict_mlogit_HH", yr),
    get(paste0("predict_mlogit_", yr)) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          -YEAR,
          ~ .x * ACS_1year_means$NHH
        )
      )
  )

  assign(
    paste0("predict_bespoke_HH", yr),
    get(paste0("predict_bespoke_", yr)) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          -YEAR,
          ~ .x * ACS_1year_means$NHH
        )
      )
  ) 
  
  assign(
    paste0("predict_ppo_HH", yr),
    get(paste0("predict_ppo_", yr)) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          -YEAR,
          ~ .x * ACS_1year_means$NHH
        )
      )
  )  
}


```

## Run chi squared tests on the distributions 

```{r}

# Chi-squared test compares the two distributions.  The test stat formula is
# Sum_{i=1}^n (Oi-Ei)^2/Ei
# Where Oi is observed number of HH in bin i, E is the estimated number of HH
# in bin i.  Sums from bin 1 to bin n which is 14 in our case. 
# compares the test-stat to the chi-squared distribution. 
# Null: the distributions are the same -> small p stat indicates they are different

results_logit_2019 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(ACS_1year_dis)), function(i) {

  obs <- unlist(ACS_1year_dis[i, -1])
  pred <- unlist(predict_logit_HH2019[i, -1])

  test <- chisq.test(
    x = obs,
    p = pred / sum(pred)
  )

  data.frame(
    Year = ACS_1year_dis$YEAR[i],
    ChiSq = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
})

print("logit chi-squared")
print(results_logit_2019)

results_mlogit_2019 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(ACS_1year_dis)), function(i) {

  obs <- unlist(ACS_1year_dis[i, -1])

  test <- chisq.test(

  )

  data.frame(
    Year = ACS_1year_dis$YEAR[i],
    ChiSq = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
})

print("mlogit chi-squared")
print(results_mlogit_2019)

results_bespoke_2019 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(ACS_1year_dis)), function(i) {

print("bespoke chi-squared")
print(results_bespoke_2019)

results_ppo_2019 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(ACS_1year_dis)), function(i) {

  obs <- unlist(ACS_1year_dis[i, -1])
```

## Regression of predictions on observed 
```{r}



years  <- c(2019, 2024)
models <- c("logit", "mlogit", "ppo", "bespoke")

model_list <- list()

## double loop across all models and all year
for (yr in years) {
  for (mdl in models) {
    
# creates a model x year list contain all input files all in wide format
# also adds a model year and a model name column to each data frame
    
    model_list[[paste0(mdl, "_", yr)]] <-
      get(paste0("predict_", mdl, "_HH", yr)) %>%
      mutate(
        model = mdl,
        model_year = yr
      )
  }
}

# binds all the wide data frames together
all_models <- bind_rows(model_list)

#pivots them into a long data frame for regressions 
all_models_long <-pivot_longer(
  data = all_models,
  cols = Inc1:Inc14,
  names_to = "IncCat",
  values_to = "predicted_HH"
)

# turns the observed distribution of HH data into a long data-frame
obsered_long <- pivot_longer(
  data = ACS_1year_dis,
  cols = Inc1:Inc14,
  names_to = "IncCat",
  values_to = "observed_HH"
)

# joins the observed data to the predicted
joined_models <- all_models_long %>% right_join(obsered_long, by=c("IncCat", "YEAR"))

#restoring ordered factor nature to the ordered factor variable
joined_models$IncCat <- ordered(joined_models$IncCat, levels = paste0("Inc", 1:14))

 # calculate RMSE step by step then combine into one step
 
 #error
 joined_models_RMSE <- joined_models %>%
   mutate(sq_error = (predicted_HH - observed_HH)^2) %>%
   filter_out(model_year==YEAR) %>%
   group_by(model) %>%
   summarise(mean_sq_error= mean(sq_error)) %>%
   mutate(RMSE = sqrt(mean_sq_error)) %>%
   select(model, RMSE) %>%
   rename(Model = model)
 
 datasummary_df(joined_models_RMSE)
```
